preamble: Diphthongization of long [uː] to [au]. In the New High German diphthongization, Middle High German ū became au [aʊ] (hūt > Haut), alongside ī > ei [aɪ] and iu > eu [ɔʏ]; in many dialects the new au fell together with the old Middle High German diphthong ou, which was lowered to au. The English Great Vowel Shift is not filed here, because it went through dated diphthong stages: Middle English /uː/ of out was /ou/ (or /əu/) about 1500 and /ɔu/ about 1600 before it reached /aʊ/.

examples.note: New High German diphthongization of Middle High German ī, ū, iu to ei, au, eu (snīden > schneiden, liute > Leute). It started in Upper Bavarian as early as the 12th century and reached Moselle Franconian only in the 16th. Alemannic (apart from Swabian) and Ripuarian keep [uː].

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). Early New High German: Phonology. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_New_High_German
